item.title: The August 1991 coup (GKChP) and Uzbekistan's independence
item.description: The coup attempt in Moscow on 19–21 August 1991 — the GKChP — shook the central Soviet authority and accelerated the union republics' declarations of independence. Ten days after the coup collapsed, on 31 August 1991 the Supreme Council of the Uzbek SSR declared state independence. This historical article covers the course of the coup, its effect on Uzbekistan, the 31 August decision, the 29 December referendum, and the dissolution of the USSR — strictly on verified sources and exact dates.

item.title: W-2 employee vs. 1099 independent contractor: worker status in the U.S.
item.description: When you work in the U.S. you are either an "employee" (W-2) or an "independent contractor" (1099) — a difference that fundamentally changes your taxes, benefits, and legal protections. This reference explains the IRS control test, Forms W-2 and 1099-NEC, FICA and self-employment tax (15.3%), quarterly taxes, worker protections, and misclassification — strictly on the basis of official sources: the IRS, SSA, and Department of Labor (DOL). This is general information, not tax or legal advice.

item.title: Getting a foreign diploma recognized in the U.S.: credential evaluation (WES, ECE, NACES)
item.description: A degree earned abroad is not automatically recognized in the United States. For an employer, university, or licensing board you will usually need a "credential evaluation" report that states what level your degree is equivalent to in the U.S. system. This reference explains what an evaluation is, the difference between document-by-document and course-by-course reports, the NACES and AICE associations, the main services (WES, ECE and others), the absence of a single federal authority, and the role in immigration — strictly on the basis of official sources. This is general information, not legal advice.

item.title: Trump urges Ukraine to elect a new leader; Zelensky proposes a 60-day ceasefire
item.description: Donald Trump criticised Zelensky over strikes on Russian refineries and said Ukraine needs a new president; Zelensky said choosing a leader is up to the Ukrainian people.

item.title: Mirziyoyev: water scarcity is an increasingly serious constraint on Central Asia's development
item.description: At the 8th Consultative Meeting in Avaza, the president of Uzbekistan called for regional cooperation on water and climate: digital monitoring, modernised irrigation, water-saving technologies, chairmanship of the Aral Sea fund, and dialogue with Afghanistan.

item.title: Mirziyoyev: water scarcity is an increasingly serious constraint on Central Asia's development
item.description: At the 8th Consultative Meeting in Avaza, the President of Uzbekistan called for regional cooperation on water losses, irrigation, climate and air pollution.

item.title: The Uzbek diaspora in Turkmenistan: the historic community of Daşoguz and Lebap
item.description: The Uzbeks of Turkmenistan are the country's largest ethnic minority. They live mainly in the northern Daşoguz and eastern Lebap provinces along the Amu Darya, and they are not recent migrants but a historically settled population. This historical reference covers the community's size (about 5–9% by source), its location, its formation from the Khiva and Bukhara khanates to the 1924–25 Soviet border delimitation, and the heritage of Köneürgench — strictly on the basis of verified sources.

item.title: Drone strikes on Russia's Yandex data centers disrupt online services in Uzbekistan
item.description: On 11 October, Ukrainian drones struck a Yandex data center in Vladimir; as a result, Yandex Go and several services were down for hours in Uzbekistan. It was the third such strike in four days.

item.title: Mirziyoyev proposes a Central Asian critical minerals alliance
item.description: At the 8th Consultative Meeting in Avaza, the President of Uzbekistan proposed accelerating a regional alliance on critical minerals and creating a unified digital map of reserves.

item.title: Drone strike on a Russian data center disrupted Yandex Go in Uzbekistan
item.description: After Ukrainian drones hit Yandex's data center in Vladimir, Yandex Go stopped working for several hours in Uzbekistan; days earlier, Uzum Market also went down.

item.title: Attack on Riyadh airport kills 12; Uzbekistan strongly condemns it
item.description: On 10 October, an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300; Uzbekistan's Foreign Ministry called it a violation of international law.

item.title: Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin: Russia to supply the US with 300,000 tonnes of fuel
item.description: US President Donald Trump announced Russia will immediately supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel — effectively reversing sanctions he signed a month earlier. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky called it a 'gift to Putin'.

item.title: Germany to allocate €71 million for projects in Uzbekistan: eight projects for 2026–2027
item.description: At intergovernmental talks in Tashkent, Germany agreed to allocate €71 million for eight projects in economic development, social protection, rule of law, climate and energy.

item.title: How to perform wudu, ghusl, and tayammum: the basics of ritual purity
item.description: Ritual purity (tahara) is a condition for prayer and many acts of worship. This reference explains, simply and chiefly according to the Hanafi school and on the basis of the Qur'an and reliable sources: the obligatory and recommended acts of wudu (ablution) and what invalidates it; when ghusl (full washing) becomes obligatory and its essentials; and tayammum, performed with clean earth when water is unavailable. This is general religious information; for specific questions consult a local imam or scholar.

item.title: January 1992: the Tashkent student protests and the price reform
item.description: On 16–17 January 1992, in the first weeks of independence, a student protest against a sharp rise in prices took place in Tashkent. Long underdocumented, the event is recorded as one of the largest open protests in independent Uzbekistan. Below, the facts of the event — its date, cause, scale, official and alternative figures on casualties, and political consequences — are presented neutrally and strictly on the basis of reputable sources.

item.title: Kremlin: Putin conveyed Iran's position on ending the conflict to Trump
item.description: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said President Vladimir Putin — in coordination with Iran's president — conveyed Tehran's views to US President Donald Trump. Iran's specific terms were not disclosed.

item.title: Houthis accuse Saudi Arabia of striking Sanaa airport; coalition says it destroyed 136 targets
item.description: Houthi-run media claimed Saudi Arabia carried out 4 strikes on Sanaa airport; the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed 136 Houthi targets. The claim and the official statement are presented separately.

item.title: Pakistan strikes Afghanistan — why Uzbekistan and its neighbors stayed silent
item.description: On 1 October Pakistan struck Kunar and Helmand provinces in Afghanistan. China, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan did not back Islamabad — Tashkent prioritizes its border and the Trans-Afghan railway.

item.title: One year of the Gaza ceasefire: strikes continue as medical sources report new deaths
item.description: 10 October 2026 marks one year of the Gaza ceasefire. Israeli strikes caused new casualties in Gaza City that day; rights groups say the truce 'exists in name only,' while Israel blames Hamas.

item.title: How asylum and the immigration court work in the United States
item.description: Asylum is a form of protection for people who fear persecution and are already in the United States or at its border. This reference explains the legal basis of asylum, who may apply, the one-year deadline and Form I-589, the two pathways (affirmative through USCIS and defensive in immigration court), the EOIR and BIA structure, work authorization, and the path to a green card and citizenship — strictly on the basis of official sources. This is general information, not legal advice.

item.title: Uzbeks in Tajikistan: the historic community of Sughd and the south
item.description: Uzbeks in Tajikistan are the country's largest ethnic minority. They are not an immigrant diaspora but a settled community that has long lived here; their position on the other side of the state border resulted from the Soviet national-territorial delimitation of 1924. The community is concentrated mainly in the north — Sughd Province, around Khujand — and in the south — Khatlon Province. Below, the community's historic roots, demographics, and changes over recent decades are presented neutrally and strictly on the basis of reputable sources.

item.title: How to build a personal budget and savings: the 50/30/20 rule and an emergency fund
item.description: A budget is a way to plan income and spending. Below, what a budget is, the 50/30/20 rule recommended by the U.S. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) — roughly 50% of income to needs, 30% to wants, and 20% to savings and debt repayment — the emergency fund (commonly three to six months of expenses), tracking spending, reducing debt, and savings accounts and compound interest are explained neutrally and strictly on the basis of official and reputable sources. This material explains mechanics; it is not financial advice.

item.title: Wildberries to build a $140 million logistics hub in Tashkent region
item.description: Russia's largest online marketplace agreed with Uzbekistan to build a 67.3-hectare hub in Zangiata district; the project will create 7,500 jobs.

item.title: Pete Hegseth says a military execution will be livestreamed to the public
item.description: The US defense secretary said the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, sentenced to death for the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, will be shown publicly; it is scheduled for December 3.

item.title: Uzbekistan: plague situation stable, no cause for concern
item.description: The sanitary-epidemiological committee reassured the public amid reports of a suspected death in Russia, saying 53 sanitary-quarantine points operate at the borders.

item.title: Uzbeks in Kyrgyzstan: the historic community of Osh and the south
item.description: Uzbeks in Kyrgyzstan are the country's largest ethnic minority (about 1 million people, roughly 15% of the population), living mainly in the south — the Osh, Jalal-Abad, and Batken provinces, in the edge of the Fergana Valley. They are not an immigrant diaspora but a settled local community: their position on the other side of the state border resulted from the Soviet national-territorial delimitation of 1924. Below, the community's historic roots, demographics, the tragic events of 1990 and 2010, and its subsequent situation are presented neutrally and strictly on the basis of reputable sources.

item.title: How credit cards work: APR, the grace period, and the minimum payment
item.description: A credit card is a tool for using revolving credit borrowed from a bank. Below, what a credit card is, the credit limit, the annual percentage rate (APR) and how interest is calculated, the grace period and how to keep it, the minimum payment and the consequence of paying only the minimum, cash advances, and how payments are allocated are explained neutrally and strictly on the basis of official sources — the U.S. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC). This material explains mechanics; it is not financial advice.

item.title: Uzbekistan is installing free solar panels for low-income families
item.description: Under the $20 million Yorqin Xonadon program, 1,580 homes and 334 public institutions have received panels; another 1,197 families will be added by 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan to prepare nine caves and a salt mine for tourism
item.description: Ten natural sites across four regions — including the Baysun caves and the Khojaikon salt mine — will be opened for tourism by 2029, with digital passports and marked routes.

item.title: Birlik and Erk: the national awakening on the eve of independence (1988–1991)
item.description: During the perestroika years a national awakening movement took shape in Uzbekistan. At its center were the Birlik (Unity) popular movement, founded on 16 November 1988 (led by Abdurahim Pulatov), and the Erk Democratic Party that grew out of it, formed in 1990 (led by Muhammad Salih). Birlik campaigned to make Uzbek the state language; that goal was achieved on 21 October 1989. Below, these movements, their demands, the presidential election of 29 December 1991, and the subsequent ban are presented neutrally and strictly on the basis of reputable sources.
